about: 10CL016 I/O tile layout relative to each pin's weak pull-up bit (io_pullup.json), same plane, in the periphery byte stream of periph.py where each logical frame holds data bytes 1..252 (byte 0 unused, 253-254 CRC): an offset past byte 252 continues at byte 1 of the next logical frame. Fitted offline on io: / iopin: / iopinq: builds.

bus_hold.evidence: pins Q, A, B (set = on; Quartus turns the pull-up off)

io_standard: LVCMOS vs LVTTL and 2.5 V change 5-8 bits in the same region (pin Q only); not generalised

open_drain.evidence: Q at PIN_T2 and 8 random pins (iox:PIN:q_od), 9/9

oe_from_core.evidence: tri-state output (iox:PIN:q_tri), 9/9; plus ~6 core routing bits for the enable

output_register: a FAST_OUTPUT_REGISTER changes only core-frame bits (13 at PIN_T2), no periphery bits; not mapped

clock_input_E2.evidence: logical periphery bits (frame, byte, plane, value) set when PIN_E2 (the Vidor 48 MHz iCLK) is a clock input: identical in div24 (X1-X3 Y6), blink24, blink24p and its 12 variants; absent in unclocked designs (cnt8, ring32). E2 is a dedicated clock pin, not in io_pullup.json.
